subtopic: Rate of a Chemical Reaction
stem:
From the concentrations of \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}\) (butyl chloride) at different times given below, calculate the average rate of the reaction:

\(\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH} + \text{HCl}\)

during different intervals of time.

| \(t/\text{s}\) | 0 | 50 | 100 | 150 | 200 | 300 | 400 | 700 | 800 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | 0.100 | 0.0905 | 0.0820 | 0.0741 | 0.0671 | 0.0549 | 0.0439 | 0.0210 | 0.017 |
solution:
We can determine the difference in concentration over different intervals of time and thus determine the average rate by dividing \(\Delta[\text{R}]\) by \(\Delta t\) (Table 3.1).

**Table 3.1: Average rates of hydrolysis of butyl chloride**

| \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_1}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_2}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | \(t_1/\text{s}\) | \(t_2/\text{s}\) | \(r_{av} \times 10^{4}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1} = -\left\{\left([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_2} - [\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_1}\right)/(t_2 - t_1)\right\} \times 10^{4}\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.100 | 0.0905 | 0 | 50 | 1.90 |
| 0.0905 | 0.0820 | 50 | 100 | 1.70 |
| 0.0820 | 0.0741 | 100 | 150 | 1.58 |
| 0.0741 | 0.0671 | 150 | 200 | 1.40 |
| 0.0671 | 0.0549 | 200 | 300 | 1.22 |
| 0.0549 | 0.0439 | 300 | 400 | 1.10 |
| 0.0439 | 0.0335 | 400 | 500 | 1.04 |
| 0.0210 | 0.017 | 700 | 800 | 0.4 |
_note: Transcribed faithfully. The book's own Table 3.1 (the printed solution) contains a row \(0.0439 \rightarrow 0.0335\) over \(400\text{-}500\,\text{s}\), but the question's data table prints NO entry at \(t = 500\,\text{s}\) and never lists the concentration 0.0335 — so that row of the solution uses data the question does not supply. Every other row is reproducible from the stem's table, and the 1.04 value is itself consistent with 0.0439/0.0335 over 100 s. Also as printed: the final concentration is given to 3 dp (0.017) where every other entry carries 4 dp.

subtopic: Rate of a Chemical Reaction
stem:
The decomposition of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) in \(\text{CCl}_4\) at 318K has been studied by monitoring the concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) in the solution. Initially the concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) is \(2.33\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\) and after 184 minutes, it is reduced to \(2.08\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\). The reaction takes place according to the equation

\(2\,\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\,(g) \rightarrow 4\,\text{NO}_2\,(g) + \text{O}_2\,(g)\)

Calculate the average rate of this reaction in terms of hours, minutes and seconds. What is the rate of production of \(\text{NO}_2\) during this period?
solution:
Average Rate \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{-\dfrac{\Delta[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{\Delta t}\right\} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{(2.08 - 2.33)\,\text{mol L}^{-1}}{184\,\text{min}}\right]\)

\(= 6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}/\text{min} = (6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}) \times (60\,\text{min}/1\text{h})\)

\(= 4.07 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}/\text{h}\)

\(= 6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1} \times 1\,\text{min}/60\,\text{s}\)

\(= 1.13 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\)

It may be remembered that

Rate \(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left\{\dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}_2]}{\Delta t}\right\}\)

\(\dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}_2]}{\Delta t} = 6.79 \times 10^{-4} \times 4\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1} = 2.72 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\)
_note: Transcribed as printed. In the fourth line of the printed solution the book writes \(6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1} \times 1\,\text{min}/60\,\text{s}\), dropping the \(\text{min}^{-1}\) that the same quantity carries two lines above; the numerical result \(1.13 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) is nevertheless correct. Also as printed: the stem describes decomposition in \(\text{CCl}_4\) solution while the equation labels every species (g).

subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
stem:
Calculate the overall order of a reaction which has the rate expression

(a) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{1/2}\,[\text{B}]^{3/2}\)

(b) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{3/2}\,[\text{B}]^{-1}\)
solution:
(a) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{x}\,[\text{B}]^{y}\)

order \(= x + y\)

So order \(= 1/2 + 3/2 = 2\), i.e., second order

(b) order \(= 3/2 + (-1) = 1/2\), i.e., half order.

subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
stem:
Identify the reaction order from each of the following rate constants.

(i) \(k = 2.3 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\)

(ii) \(k = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}^{-1}\)
solution:
(i) The unit of second order rate constant is \(\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), therefore \(k = 2.3 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) represents a second order reaction.

(ii) The unit of a first order rate constant is \(\text{s}^{-1}\) therefore \(k = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}^{-1}\) represents a first order reaction.

subtopic: Integrated Rate Equations
stem: The initial concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) in the following first order reaction \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g) \rightarrow 2\,\text{NO}_2(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g)\) was \(1.24 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\) at \(318\,\text{K}\). The concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) after 60 minutes was \(0.20 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\). Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at \(318\,\text{K}\).
solution:
For a first order reaction

\(\log\dfrac{[\text{R}]_1}{[\text{R}]_2} = \dfrac{k(t_2 - t_1)}{2.303}\)

\(k = \dfrac{2.303}{(t_2 - t_1)}\log\dfrac{[\text{R}]_1}{[\text{R}]_2}\)

\(= \dfrac{2.303}{(60\,\text{min} - 0\,\text{min})}\log\dfrac{1.24 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}}{0.20 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}}\)

\(= \dfrac{2.303}{60}\log 6.2\;\text{min}^{-1}\)

\(k = 0.0304\,\text{min}^{-1}\)

subtopic: Integrated Rate Equations
stem:
The following data were obtained during the first order thermal decomposition of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g)\) at constant volume:

\(2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g) \rightarrow 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) + \text{O}_2(g)\)

| S.No. | Time/s | Total Pressure/(atm) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | \(0\) | \(0.5\) |
| 2. | \(100\) | \(0.512\) |

Calculate the rate constant.
solution:
Let the pressure of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g)\) decrease by \(2x\) atm. As two moles of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) decompose to give two moles of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\) and one mole of \(\text{O}_2(g)\), the pressure of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\) increases by \(2x\) atm and that of \(\text{O}_2(g)\) increases by \(x\) atm.

| | \(2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(g)\) | \(2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)\) | \(\text{O}_2(g)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start \(t = 0\) | \(0.5\) atm | \(0\) atm | \(0\) atm |
| At time \(t\) | \((0.5 - 2x)\) atm | \(2x\) atm | \(x\) atm |

\(p_t = p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_5} + p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_4} + p_{\text{O}_2}\)

\(= (0.5 - 2x) + 2x + x = 0.5 + x\)

\(x = p_t - 0.5\)

\(p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_5} = 0.5 - 2x = 0.5 - 2(p_t - 0.5) = 1.5 - 2p_t\)

At \(t = 100\,\text{s}\); \(p_t = 0.512\,\text{atm}\)

\(p_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_5} = 1.5 - 2 \times 0.512 = 0.476\,\text{atm}\)

Using equation (3.16)

\(k = \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log\dfrac{p_i}{p_A} = \dfrac{2.303}{100\,\text{s}}\log\dfrac{0.5\,\text{atm}}{0.476\,\text{atm}}\)

\(= \dfrac{2.303}{100\,\text{s}} \times 0.0216 = 4.98 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}^{-1}\)

subtopic: Integrated Rate Equations
stem: A first order reaction is found to have a rate constant, \(k = 5.5 \times 10^{-14}\,\text{s}^{-1}\). Find the half-life of the reaction.
solution:
Half-life for a first order reaction is

\(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}\)

\(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{5.5 \times 10^{-14}\,\text{s}^{-1}} = 1.26 \times 10^{13}\,\text{s}\)

subtopic: Integrated Rate Equations
stem: Show that in a first order reaction, time required for completion of 99.9% is 10 times of half-life \((t_{1/2})\) of the reaction.
solution:
When reaction is completed 99.9%, \([\text{R}]_n = [\text{R}]_0 - 0.999[\text{R}]_0\)

\(k = \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log\dfrac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\)

\(= \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log\dfrac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]_0 - 0.999[\text{R}]_0} = \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log 10^{3}\)

\(t = 6.909/k\)

For half-life of the reaction

\(t_{1/2} = 0.693/k\)

\(\dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{6.909}{k} \times \dfrac{k}{0.693} = 10\)
_note: Transcribed as printed. The book writes the concentration remaining after 99.9% completion as \([\text{R}]_n\) in the opening line, then uses plain \([\text{R}]\) for that same quantity in the log expression on the very next line — an internal notation inconsistency in the printed solution, not a change of meaning.

stem: The rate constants of a reaction at 500K and 700K are \(0.02\,\text{s}^{-1}\) and \(0.07\,\text{s}^{-1}\) respectively. Calculate the values of \(E_a\) and \(A\).
_note: Transcribed exactly as printed on p-20; three defects in the book's own printed solution. (1) The last step prints A = 0.02/0.012 = 1.61, but that division evaluates to 1.67. The book displays the exponential rounded to 0.012 while dividing by the unrounded value e^(-4.386) = 0.01243, which does give 1.61 — so the stated answer is right and the displayed arithmetic does not reproduce it. (2) E_a is printed as 18230.8 J with the per-mole dropped; it should be J mol^-1, since R was used as J K^-1 mol^-1. (3) A is printed without units; for a first-order reaction it carries s^-1. The R units in THIS example are printed correctly as J K^-1 mol^-1 (unlike Eg 3.10 — see its note).

subtopic: Temperature Dependence of the Rate of a Reaction
stem:
The first order rate constant for the decomposition of ethyl iodide by the reaction

\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{I(g)} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{(g)} + \text{HI(g)}\)

at 600K is \(1.60 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{s}^{-1}\). Its energy of activation is \(209\,\text{kJ/mol}\). Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at 700K.
_note: The stem is on p-20 and the solution finishes on p-21 (band boundary); both halves are transcribed here. PRINTED-UNIT FAULT in the substitution line on p-21, confirmed at 3x magnification: the book prints the numerator as '209000 J mol L^-1' and the denominator as '2.303 x 8.314 J mol L^-1 K^-1' — a stray litre where the superscript -1 on 'mol' belongs. As printed those units are chemically impossible (R is J mol^-1 K^-1). Per the chemistry brief's rendered-glyph-fault rule the INTENDED units are transcribed (J mol^-1 and J mol^-1 K^-1) rather than the printed ones, so the stored solution does not teach a wrong unit for R. The same book prints the units correctly in Eg 3.9 one page earlier.

(ii) \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(aq) + 3\text{I}^-(aq) + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{I}_3^-\)   Rate \(= k[\text{H}_2\text{O}_2][\text{I}^-]\)

(iii) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_4(g) + \text{CO}(g)\)   Rate \(= k[\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}]^{3/2}\)

(iv) \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}(g) \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{HCl}(g)\)   Rate \(= k[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}]\)
_note: Sub-item (i) is printed exactly as shown and is NOT balanced: the left side carries 3 N and 3 O, the right side 2 N and 1 O (the usual form of this reaction is \(3\text{NO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O} + \text{NO}_2\)). stem: Sucrose decomposes in acid solution into glucose and fructose according to the first order rate law, with \(t_{1/2} = 3.00\) hours. What fraction of sample of sucrose remains after 8 hours ?

stem:
The decomposition of hydrocarbon follows the equation

\(k = (4.5 \times 10^{11}\,\text{s}^{-1})\,e^{-28000\,\text{K}/T}\)

Calculate \(E_a\).

stem:
The rate constant for the first order decomposition of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\) is given by the following equation:

\(\log k = 14.34 - 1.25 \times 10^{4}\,\text{K}/T\)

Calculate \(E_a\) for this reaction and at what temperature will its half-period be 256 minutes?
